claims: "Buffalo" most commonly refers to the American bison (Bison bison).
American bison (Bison bison) is a large, hump-backed, shaggy-maned bovid native to North America.
American bison is often erroneously called buffalo.
True buffaloes are African buffalo or Asian water buffalo.
African buffalo and Asian water buffalo belong to different genera.
American bison have a shaggy brown coat.
American bison have a large shoulder hump.
American bison have short, curved horns.
American bison weigh up to 2,000 pounds.
American bison once ranged from Alaska to Mexico.
American bison today live in highly fragmented herds in national parks, wildlife refuges, and private ranches in the U.S. and Canada.
American bison are herbivores.
American bison feed on grasses, weeds, and leafy plants.
American bison were once near extinction.
Conservation efforts have established numerous herds of American bison.
The scientific name of African buffalo is Syncerus caffer.
African buffalo are found in Sub-Saharan Africa.
African buffalo have a near-threatened conservation status.
The scientific name of water buffalo is Bubalus bubalis.
Water buffalo are primarily domesticated in Asia for labor and dairy.
Wild water buffalo are highly endangered.
Bison have shorter, sharper, black horns designed for fighting.
African buffalo have larger, curved horns that form a "boss" or shield.
Buffalo do not have a prominent shoulder hump.
The American bison is the national mammal of the United States.
American bison are known as tatanka in Lakota.
American bison were vital for food, clothing, and shelter for many Indigenous peoples.
